findings.classification: reproduced introduced static-guard false negative; not a native API or browser outcome finding
findings.title: The native next exception accepts output mutations that discard the continuation
findings.trigger: Build {items: page.items, next: page.next}, then mutate projected.next, overwrite the enclosing spread next, or use Object.assign to replace next. The input page stays untouched.
findings.expected: A lossy projected next must retain a dropped-continuation finding. A safe local proof may conservatively refuse an unverified output lifetime.
findings.actual: All three programs return the original items with next=null despite a non-null opaque input token. The parent scanner reports dropped-continuation for each page.items; the candidate returns an empty inventory for all three. Each candidate case reaches and fails the guard outcome assertion.
findings.cause: stableNativeEnvelope traverses uses rooted at the input identifier page and treats the inner object property values as forwarded. The exemption checks only that inner literal. Neither the projected binding mutation nor an outer spread/Object.assign overwrite is a page-rooted use, and next is not included in the existing continuations set that independently flags assignments. Keeping the input envelope stable does not prove the returned projection keeps its continuation.
findings.classScope: Three output-lifetime variants were checked together against the exact same scanner blobs. No new current production instance or native data-loss journey is claimed.
findings.requestedFix: G-2758 should keep the exception conservative unless the projected output itself is proven to escape intact; cover binding mutation/alias and enclosing overrides with additive controls. Preserve all original planted refusals, inventories and actual red production assertions. Do not broaden acceptance by helper/type/path name.
